chunks: I certainly saw 'Aqil fallen in destitution to the point that he asked me for a sa' of your wheat, and I saw his children with dishevelled hair and dusty colors due to their poverty, as if their faces had been blackened with indigo. He renewed his request to me emphatically, and repeated the saying to me repeatedly, so I directed my hearing to him, and he thought that I would sell him my religion and follow his lead, leaving my own way. So I heated a piece of iron for him, then brought it near his body so that he might take a lesson from it, then he cried with the cry of one suffering from a chronic ailment due to its pain, and he was about to burn from its branding.

key_terms.اسْتَمَاحَنِي: He asked me for something (implies asking for a specific amount or item)
key_terms.ذِي دَنَفٍ: One suffering from a chronic/lingering ailment
key_terms.صَاعًا: A sa', a unit of volume/weight approx. 3kg

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) handle his brother Aqil's repeated requests for money?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employed a pragmatic strategy of 'controlled generosity' by branding 'Aqil with iron to create a visible mark of poverty, thereby preventing him from repeatedly asking for more while preserving the Imam's dignity and resources. This incident highlights the Shia scholarly understanding of balancing familial duty with political and economic prudence, illustrating how physical discipline was used as a pedagogical tool to teach patience and reduce dependency.
